chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abi Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The traveler does not pray behind the resident; if he prains, he should dismiss himself (complete his prayer) in two rak'ahs.'

key_terms.اَلْمُسَافِرُ: The traveler (one on a journey with specific prayer rules)
key_terms.اَلْمُقِيمُ: The resident (one not on a journey)

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do if he prays behind a resident?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural nuance of a traveler praying behind a resident, emphasizing that the traveler must shorten their prayer to two rak'ahs even if they initially follow the resident's four-rak'ah prayer. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the *musafir* in congregational settings, ensuring the integrity of the shortened prayer structure as prescribed in Shia jurisprudence.
